newsitem.title: USA: Marriott CEO sees fewer industry players.
newsitem.headline: Marriott CEO sees fewer industry players.

text.p: The head of Marriott International Inc forecast there would be more and more consolidation in the lodging sector, with only a few large companies making up the future of the industry.
"We see a great consolidation going on," Chairman J.W. Marriott Jr said at the company's annual meeting here. "We think there'll end up being just a few big players in the industry."
Marriott said the industry's consolidation has been driven in part by "the things you have to do to remain competitive."
Speaking at a briefing after the shareholders' meeting, he cited the pressure to expand into global markets and the cost of technology as key reasons for the consolidation.

At the meeting, Marriott said he plans to remain a "very active" chairman and chief executive officer, despite the official appointment of a new president six weeks ago in preparation for "a smooth transition to the next generation of leadership."
He added: "I'm not leaving. I'm not retiring."

In response to a shareholder question, Marriott defended the company's payment of $1 billion earlier this year to acquire Renaissance Hotel Group, a deal that allowed Marriott to double its international presence in lodging.
"It was a very heated auction right up until the very last morning," Marriott said. "We don't think that we overpaid. We think we paid a full price."
In his formal remarks, Marriott said the company plans to expand its existing brands, services and businesses, as well as acquire or develop new ones.
"We will continue our tradition of being a growth company," he said. "We will also continue to emphasize global expansion, planting the Marriott flag in more spots around the world."
He noted that, even with the acquisition of Renaissance, Marriott operates or franchises just seven percent of the U.S. lodging market and only two percent worldwide.
"Clearly, we have plenty of room to grow," he said.

Senior living remains another strong area of growth, with the company planning to operate more than 200 communities by the year 2000. Its resort timeshare business is also a growth target, with the company expecting to double the number of ownership intervals sold annually over the next five years.
Marriott said the company also aims to sustain double-digit annual growth in its management services business by selling existing clients additional services and by adding new clients.
